A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DGSim research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original rigid-body, elastic, and cloth simulation experiments, quantitative comparisons, six ablation studies, and qualitative generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a fine-tuned comparator, additional evaluation scores, and qualitative rollout examples.

M1.justification: The reported objective changes future-loss weighting from gamma^k in v1 Equation 9 to gamma^(k-T-1) in v2 Equation 8, changing its balance against past reconstruction at fixed lambda. The core architecture remains intact. Newly specified FiLM conditioning elaborates v1's geometrically conditioned feature network; the PDFs do not establish an architectural replacement or experimental reruns.

E1.justification: The three datasets, object lists, and principal dynamics tasks remain unchanged. Appendix C.1 additionally demonstrates higher-throw and parallel-composition scenes, modestly extending the explicitly documented test scenarios beyond v1's ground edits and multi-object collisions.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates only the pretrained Cosmos-1.0-Autoregressive-5B-Video2World external comparator. v2 retains it and adds CosmosFT, a dataset-specific LoRA fine-tuned Cosmos-Predict2 2B model, across all three datasets in Figure 11. This substantially strengthens comparator coverage with an adapted model. Other particle simulators discussed in Table 1 remain unevaluated.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a 6,000-iteration LoRA protocol for CosmosFT and adds LPIPS as an evaluation metric. It also revises the stated elastic/cloth depth range from [15, 8] to [1.5, 8]. The held-out fraction, principal 3DGSim training budgets, and camera protocols remain unchanged. SSIM was already mentioned in v1, although its scores were absent.

E4.justification: All six systematic ablations are retained unchanged, moving from v1 Appendix A to v2 Appendix B. Appendix C adds qualitative case-study evidence for editing and composability, including higher throws, parallel simulation, and five-worm interactions. The ordinary dataset rollout gallery does not constitute additional ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions use plus/minus values and shaded trajectory plots without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance procedures. v2 applies the existing reporting practice to additional rows and metrics; no changed statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Existing PSNR entries and all six ablation tables retain their values. v2 Figure 11 adds CosmosFT future PSNR results of 26.44, 26.50, and 22.49 for rigid, elastic, and cloth respectively, plus SSIM and LPIPS throughout the comparison. Appendix C supplies additional qualitative outcomes. These substantially expand the evidence without establishing a same-setting improvement in 3DGSim performance.

T1.justification: The loss definition changes non-equivalently: v2 Equation 8 gives the first future frame discount 1, whereas v1 Equation 9 gives gamma^(T+1). This is a limited mathematical correction. Serialization and temporal-merging mathematics are retained, including material relocated to Appendix A.2; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain end-to-end learning from multi-view RGB, latent particle representations, transformer dynamics with temporal encoding and merging, Gaussian rendering, and generalization across rigid, elastic, cloth, and edited scenes. v2 reorganizes and emphasizes these contributions without substantially changing their scientific meaning or scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability qualifications: scarce multi-view data, no explicit occlusion handling, and real-world validation remaining future work, explicitly framing the study as a proof of concept. Its Benchmarking discussion also acknowledges the single-view versus multi-view comparison mismatch. These considerably qualify v1's broadly optimistic generalization discussion; existing camera-failure and ground-penetration observations remain.

D1.justification: v2 identifies AdamW, details FiLM conditioning, specifies the conditioning CNN's layers, channels, kernel and activation, and gives the particle-wise MLP dimensions in Appendix A. It also adds a project access link. These supplement v1's already extensive hyperparameter and hardware disclosures; they do not establish that the underlying implementation changed.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around privileged supervision, temporal correspondence, and analytical physics priors. It adds discussion and citations for compositional NeRF dynamics, DPI-Net, VGGT, MASt3R-SLAM, FiLM, and physics-based Gaussian methods, while removing several traditional-simulator references. Table 1 and the new Benchmarking passage additionally distinguish resource availability and explain comparator selection.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces separate Preliminaries, State Representation, and View-Independent Inverse Renderer sections, moves detailed PTv3 exposition into Appendix A.2, and reorganizes supplementary material into implementation details, ablations, and visualizations.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a predominantly single-column layout, redraws the overview, adds a feature-decomposition diagram and speed chart, and expands the main results display with comparator rows and metric columns. It relocates the original teaser and retained ablation tables and adds the extensive Appendix C gallery. The expanded results table is captioned Figure 11 and rendered considerably smaller.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's PSNR-only reported comparison, v2's adapted comparator and SSIM/LPIPS results provide more informative empirical evidence. Appendix A improves implementation transparency, and the new limitations clarify applicability. These benefits outweigh the denser, harder-to-read results table, but unmatched comparator inputs, limited fine-tuning details, and absent real-world validation remain. The overall gain is useful but limited.
